articles.title: Cowboys owner Jerry Jones gets a lesson on how to become a real ‘pimp’
articles.summary: Jerry Jones has spent decades running the Dallas Cowboys, but apparently there was still one important skill he needed to master.
articles.body:
Jerry Jones has spent decades running the Dallas Cowboys, but apparently there was still one important skill he needed to master.

When Michael Irvin spotted the Cowboys owner with his new cane at training camp, The Playmaker decided Jerry needed a lesson on how to properly walk with it.

And Irvin didn't just explain it. He demonstrated the full “pimp walk,” showing Jones the rhythm, the swagger and exactly how to move with the cane.

Jerry immediately tried to copy him, turning Cowboys training camp into one of the funniest lessons of the preseason.

Three Super Bowls together apparently weren't enough. More than 30 years later, Irvin is still teaching his old boss new tricks.

articles.title: Von Miller joins the Cowboys with outrageous demands: Offer to team's star player for jersey number
articles.standfirst: The veteran pass rusher wants his old number back and has come up with a memorable price
articles.summary: The veteran pass rusher wants his old number back and has come up with a memorable price
articles.body:
After years of talking about what it would mean to play for the team he grew up supporting, Von Miller has finally landed with the Dallas Cowboys . His first problem in Texas, however, has nothing to do with learning the defense or getting back into football shape. It's No.40.

That number currently belongs to fullback Hunter Luepke , and Miller has already started lobbying for it with an offer that is difficult to forget.

“I don’t know what uniform I’mma be. I know, you know, Hunter is 40,” Miller said. “I’m not going to get caught up in the number, but I did make some offers to him already that he can’t really, you know, come off of those. I think, you know, a lifetime supply of chicken would do it.”

The chicken would presumably come from Miller’s Green Patcher’s operation in Texas, making the proposal more than just a throwaway joke.

Why No.40 matters to Von Miller

Miller has worn several numbers during an NFL career that already includes two Super Bowl championships, eight Pro Bowl selections and three first-team All-Pro honors.

His most famous years came in No.58 with the Denver Broncos , but No. 40 has followed him through multiple chapters. He wore it at Texas A&M, then again with the Los Angeles Rams and Buffalo Bills .

Last season with the Washington Commanders , Miller wore No.24.

One number he has already ruled out in Dallas is No.94. Miller has said he does not want to wear the number most associated with DeMarcus Ware, the former Cowboys pass-rushing great.

That makes No.40 the natural target, assuming Luepke can be persuaded. A lifetime supply of chicken might at least get the conversation moving.

Cowboys taking time with Miller on the field

The jersey number has provided a light moment, but the Cowboys are being cautious with Miller ’s football workload.

He joined the team in the middle of training camp and has not played since January 4, meaning there is little reason to rush a 36-year-old veteran with 14 NFL seasons behind him.

“We’re not gonna rush him out there,” head coach Brian Schottenheimer said. “There’s no need to do that. It’s more about getting him around the fellas, getting him with Christian Parker and the defensive staff.”

That transition should be helped by Christian Parker ’s familiarity with Miller from their time together in Denver.

The Cowboys are adding a player who recorded nine sacks with the Commanders last season and still believes he can make an impact for a contender.

The bigger priority will be making sure Miller is ready when the regular season begins. Still, if his jersey negotiation goes the way he hopes, No.40 could soon come with the most unusual payment plan in the NFL.

articles.title: The Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders take the city by storm with concert alongside Megan Moroney
articles.standfirst: A performance of “Am I Okay?” became a hometown spectacle when Moroney unveiled her surprise guests
articles.summary: A performance of “Am I Okay?” became a hometown spectacle when Moroney unveiled her surprise guests
articles.body:
Megan Moroney knew exactly where she was performing when her Cloud 9 Tour rolled into Dallas.

What initially looked like another packed stop on the country star’s growing tour became something much more specific to Texas when the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders suddenly appeared alongside her.

The surprise came at American Airlines Center on August 14 as Moroney performed her 2024 hit “Am I Okay?". The cheerleaders joined the performance, adding their unmistakable choreography to a song already familiar to much of the crowd.

It was the kind of guest appearance that made sense only in Dallas. Moroney leaned into the moment rather than allowing the cheerleaders to become a brief sideshow, creating a crossover between country music and one of the NFL’s most recognizable institutions.

The reaction continued after the show. The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders shared photographs from the performance and their time with Moroney backstage, writing: “Head in the pink country clouds last night. Best day ever with our girl, @megmoroney!”

Moroney responded with an equally enthusiastic tribute alongside her own photos: “God bless the girls.”

Megan Moroney takes the Cowboys theme beyond the surprise

Bringing out the cheerleaders wasn’t the only nod Moroney made to Dallas.

The singer later appeared in a custom dress decorated with Cowboys-inspired rhinestones for her final song, “Six Months Later,” carrying the local theme through to the end of the concert. Footage from behind the scenes also showed her spending time with the cheerleaders away from the performance itself.

That attention to detail helped distinguish Dallas from the other stops on Moroney’s tour.

The appearance also arrived as the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders prepared for their own return to NFL action. While the Dallas Cowboys opened their preseason away from home, the cheerleaders are scheduled to be back at AT&T Stadium when Dallas hosts the New Orleans Saints in its lone home preseason game on August 28.

The Cowboys then open their regular-season home schedule against the Washington Commanders on September 20.

Cloud 9 Tour prepares to leave the United States

Moroney’s Dallas spectacle came during the later stages of the American portion of her Cloud 9 Tour, which began in May following the release of her album Cloud 9.

The schedule takes her through several more U.S. cities before the production heads overseas in September. European dates include Oslo, Stockholm, Cologne, Tilburg and Paris, followed by shows in London and Manchester before the tour concludes in Belfast in October.

Those audiences will get the full Cloud 9 experience, but replicating what happened in Dallas could prove difficult.

The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders' appearance gave “Am I Okay?” a hometown identity that belonged specifically to that crowd, while Moroney’s Cowboys-themed finale completed the transformation.

One of the biggest cheers of the evening ultimately came when two distinctly American entertainment worlds collided on the same Dallas stage.

articles.title: Jake Ferguson faces a big challenge to make Haley Cavinder and their “baby” happy on Valentine’s Day
articles.standfirst: The puppy’s post sparked a fun question ahead of February.
articles.summary: The puppy’s post sparked a fun question ahead of February.
articles.body:
Haley Cavinder and Jake Ferguson are still enjoying their first few months as newlyweds , but it seems someone at home is already thinking about what comes next. A recent post put Boozer , the couple’s “fur baby,” back in front of the cameras and offered a small hint about what could become one of the family’s most anticipated moments of 2027 .

A football changed the message completely

In the video, Boozer can be seen playing with a football while a question appears on screen: “Valentine’s Day plans?”

The answer comes immediately afterward and is written from the puppy’s perspective: “Watching my dad in the Super Bowl . Try again next year. #HowBoutThemBoys”.

The message turns a sweet post into a direct reference to Jake and the Dallas Cowboys. Boozer, in other words, has already decided how he wants to spend the next Valentine’s Day .

Now, there is one pretty important thing left: his "dad" has to make it to that game.

The Super Bowl will take place on February 14

Super Bowl LXI is scheduled for February 14, 2027 , meaning the game and Valentine’s Day will fall on the same date.

For Boozer, apparently, there is not much to think about. While other couples might be planning a romantic celebration, he already seems ready to cheer for Jake.

Of course, the message comes with a healthy dose of humor. No one can know yet which teams will make it to the Super Bowl, and Dallas will have to get through the entire regular season and playoffs to reach that stage .

Jake Ferguson has his own challenge ahead

The tight end finished the 2025 season with 82 receptions and eight touchdowns , a level of production that raised expectations for his next campaign.

Now he will have to look to maintain or improve those numbers and become an even more important piece in helping Dallas reach its goals. Will he do it?

articles.title: Camden Brown keeps hitting big plays and makes Brian Schottenheimer's decision even harder
articles.standfirst: The undrafted rookie wide receiver is making a serious push for a spot on the 53-man roster.
articles.summary: The undrafted rookie wide receiver is making a serious push for a spot on the 53-man roster.
articles.body:
Every preseason, there are always one or two players who become fan favorites. They don't always end up making the 53-man roster to start the season, but their underdog stories are impossible to not sympathize with.

This year, that's very much Camden Brown for the Dallas Cowboys . Brown was an undrafted free agent before joining the Cowboys, having had an unconventional college football career. He failed to make an impact in three seasons at Auburn , but exploded with a 65/1,079/14 season at Georgia Southern in his final collegiate year.

Camden Brown is making a serious case to be on Dallas Cowboys 53-man roster

After a strong summer period with the team, Brown made the most of his opportunity in Dallas' first preseason game. He caught three passes for 62 yards, with two of those turning into touchdowns .

On Saturday, Brown was at it again making big plays. In the second quarter of the team's game against the Arizona Cardinals , Brown got loose for a 70-yard reception that nearly ended with another touchdown.

Brown's ascension makes head coach Brian Schottenheimer and the front office's final cut decisions very difficult. CeeDee Lamb , George Pickens , Ryan Flournoy , and Kavontae Turpin are roster locks. Marquez Valdes-Scantling is probably safe, too, and Jonathan Mingo scored a 53-yard touchdown in that same Cardinals game.

With those six in place, it would be surprising if the Cowboys ended up keeping seven wide receivers on the 53-man roster . That would leave Brown as the odd man out, with the hope of sneaking him through waivers onto the practice squad. But given his preseason performances, he would likely get scooped up before he made it back to the Cowboys.

articles.title: Was he targeted? Thieves steal $300,000 worth of luxury goods from CeeDee Lamb's home during Cowboys training camp
articles.standfirst: A break-in at the Cowboys receiver’s house highlights a troubling trend affecting professional athletes
articles.summary: A break-in at the Cowboys receiver’s house highlights a troubling trend affecting professional athletes
articles.body:
CeeDee Lamb was preparing for another season as one of the Dallas Cowboys ’ biggest offensive weapons when criminals targeted his Texas home, stealing more than $300,000 worth of luxury items while he was away at training camp.

The burglary happened at Lamb ’s residence in Fairview, Texas, while the wide receiver was with the Cowboys in Oxnard, California.

According to police records, the break-in was discovered on July 31 after a worker assisting with renovations near the property noticed a broken window.

After checking the home and finding evidence of a burglary, the worker contacted authorities. Police later determined that the intruder had entered through the damaged window and taken several expensive belongings, including four luxury bags.

No suspects have been identified, and the Fairview Police Department continues to investigate the incident. The break-in adds Lamb ’s name to a growing list of professional athletes who have had their homes targeted while away from their properties.

NFL players increasingly targeted

Home burglaries involving NFL stars have become an increasing concern in recent years, with criminals often targeting players when they are traveling for games, practices or other team activities.

Along with Lamb , several high-profile players have experienced similar incidents, including Patrick Mahomes, Joe Burrow and Shedeur Sanders . Cowboys defensive tackle Linval Joseph also had his home burglarized in 2024.

The NFL responded to the rise in incidents by issuing a security alert warning players that organized groups were using public information, social media posts and team schedules to track when homes were likely to be empty.

The league advised players to limit sharing their locations online, strengthen home security measures and avoid publicly displaying valuable possessions.

While many previous burglaries occurred during games when players were away, Lamb ’s case shows that criminals are also taking advantage of extended absences, such as training camps.

Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott recently spoke about the challenges that come with being a high-profile athlete and how public success can create security risks.

“Not everything that comes with it [fame] is great,” Prescott said. “You weigh the good with the bad. What we’re subject to, that others can look up and just see how much we make or maybe an address, and that puts us subject to a target.”

Lamb keeps focus on Cowboys season

The burglary comes as Lamb enters another important season with Dallas, continuing to establish himself as one of the NFL’s elite wide receivers.

Despite dealing with an ankle injury during the 2025 season, Lamb still surpassed 1,000 receiving yards for the fifth consecutive year, remaining a key part of the Cowboys ’ offensive plans.

He has also built a strong relationship with new teammate George Pickens , with Prescott praising the pair for their chemistry and willingness to put the team ahead of individual success.

“Just their personalities, they’re truly unselfish,” Prescott said. “They truly want the other guy to have just as much success as each of them has individually; they’re cheering each other on.”

The Cowboys are preparing for their season opener against the New York Giants , while Lamb waits for authorities to complete their investigation.

The incident is another reminder of the unique challenges faced by professional athletes, where fame and financial success can also bring unwanted attention away from the field.

articles.title: The departure of three of the Dallas Cowboys' most beloved cheerleaders has left the team deeply shaken
articles.standfirst: America’s Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders will return for a fourth season, but fans will have to get used to seeing some familiar faces missing from the lineup
articles.summary: America’s Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders will return for a fourth season, but fans will have to get used to seeing some familiar faces missing from the lineup
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders are preparing for another season in the spotlight, but the return of Netflix's America’s Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders will come with a bittersweet change.

Season 4 has officially been confirmed for 2027, with Netflix once again taking viewers behind the scenes of auditions, training camp and the NFL season.

However, the new episodes will feature a substantially different group of dancers after several popular members of the squad decided to move on.

Among the most significant departures are Reece Weaver, Megan McElaney and Kleine Powell , three cheerleaders who became especially recognizable to viewers through the first three seasons of the Netflix documentary series.

Their exits mean that the fourth season will have to establish a new group of personalities while continuing the stories of returning veterans.

Reece's departure has perhaps generated the biggest reaction. She became one of the faces most closely associated with America’s Sweethearts, having joined the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders as a rookie during the same season the Netflix series debuted.

Her three-season journey included some of the show's most memorable personal and professional moments.

Unlike many dancers who remain with the organization for several years, Reece chose to leave after three seasons. She subsequently secured a major new opportunity, with a Broadway debut in Chicago marking the next stage of her career.

“I don't think I’ve ever been more nervous before in my life,” Reece recalled of the day she announced her retirement. “The scary part is I don’t know where I’m landing, and so it’s just about going into the unknown.”

Her decision was particularly emotional because she had become synonymous with the Netflix series.

Three familiar faces are moving on

Megan McElaney and Kleine Powell are also leaving the DCC after lengthy runs with the organization. Both had reached the five-year mark, making their departures part of the natural cycle of life on one of the NFL's most demanding cheerleading squads.

Megan finished her DCC career on an especially high note, earning Veteran of the Year honors and serving as a group leader during her final season. Kleine had likewise established herself as a veteran presence before stepping away.

The departures don't mean the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders are short of recognizable personalities, however.

Several familiar dancers remain, including Charly Barby , who was highlighted in Netflix's Season 4 announcement, as well as other returning veterans. The 2026-27 roster also includes eight new rookies, creating a mixture of established stars and newcomers.

Two of the most important figures behind the scenes will also remain. Senior director Kelli Finglass and head choreographer Judy Trammell are both returning, ensuring that the show's central leadership remains intact.

Finglass welcomed another opportunity to showcase the dancers and their individual journeys.

“Each new season is another opportunity to showcase the extraordinary talent, dedication and individuality of our team,” she said.

“We’re proud to continue to share their stories and artistry with audiences, inspiring the next generation of young performers all over the world to dream big and pursue their passions.”

The changes are a reminder of just how quickly the DCC landscape can evolve. America’s Sweethearts follows the cheerleaders from auditions through training camp and the football season, meaning viewers become invested not only in the performances but also in the individual women behind the uniforms.

That emotional investment is precisely why the departures of Reece , Megan and Kleine have landed so heavily with fans.

Still, their exits also create an opportunity for the fourth season to introduce a new generation of fan favorites. Several former cut candidates have already returned to training camp, while the new rookie class will get its chance to establish itself in front of Netflix's enormous audience.

Netflix has not yet announced an exact premiere date for Season 4, although the series is expected to return in 2027.

The new season will follow the 2026-27 DCC campaign, meaning viewers can expect another mixture of auditions, intense preparation, football performances and personal stories.

For longtime viewers, however, one thing will be impossible to ignore: the fourth season will look noticeably different without three of the show's most familiar faces.

Reece, Megan and Kleine may have left the squad, but their impact on America’s Sweethearts is likely to remain part of the show's identity for years to come.

Apparently, building Cowboys chemistry sometimes starts with learning a few dance moves.

articles.title: Brian Schottenheimer’s 2026 roster reality check sends Cowboys Super Bowl hopes sky-high
articles.standfirst: Brian Schottenheimer believes the Cowboys are a completely different team in 2026.
articles.summary: Brian Schottenheimer believes the Cowboys are a completely different team in 2026.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are starting to generate excitement ahead of the 2026 season. After a convincing 34-13 victory over the Arizona Cardinals in the preseason, Brian Schottenheimer ’s team is looking to carry that momentum into the start of the campaign when they face the New York Giants in Week 1 on September 13 .

Beyond the result, the strongest message came from the head coach himself, who stated that the current version of the Cowboys is better than the one that finished last season. Schottenheimer highlighted significant improvements in roster talent and depth, two areas he believes are essential to competing at the highest level.

“If you take our roster from last year and you lay it down next to our roster from this year, there’s no question that the depth and the overall talent is higher,” Schottenheimer said, according to Jon Machota of The Athletic . “This is a good football team. We got a lot of confidence. We just got to make the right decisions as we get to cut-down day, which we will.”

The optimism in Dallas starts with an offense loaded with talent. Dak Prescott remains the leader of the unit, while the quarterback will have weapons such as CeeDee Lamb and new addition George Pickens , a receiver duo that could provide more explosiveness to the passing game.

The biggest focus, however, is on a defense that needs a major turnaround after an inconsistent season. The Cowboys strengthened their defensive line with players like Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark , hoping to raise the level of a unit that was one of the team’s biggest weaknesses.

Dallas finished last season with a 7-9 record, placing second in the NFC East and falling short of the expectations surrounding the franchise. Now, with a roster that Schottenheimer believes is more complete, the Cowboys will look to prove they are ready to compete among the NFL’s elite once again.

articles.title: Sell high: Why the Cowboys should explore a Joe Milton trade right now
articles.standfirst: The young quarterback checks many of the boxes that intrigue personnel executives
articles.summary: The young quarterback checks many of the boxes that intrigue personnel executives
articles.body:
J oe Milton III may have delivered the most exciting performance of the Dallas Cowboys’ preseason , but that doesn’t mean the franchise should keep him. In fact, Milton’s breakout showing against the Arizona Cardinals may have created the perfect opportunity for Dallas to capitalize on his rising value before reality catches up with expectations.

The young quarterback was electric in the Cowboys’ 34-13 preseason victory, completing 9 of 13 passes for 179 yards and two touchdowns while adding a rushing score. He looked confident, decisive, and far more comfortable than he did earlier in his NFL career. For a player who entered the league with questions about his consistency and development, it was exactly the type of performance that gets front offices around the league paying attention.

But while many Cowboys fans are wondering whether Milton has done enough to secure the backup quarterback job behind Dak Prescott, Dallas should be asking a different question: Can this performance help bring back valuable assets in a trade? The answer may be yes.

Milton's value may never be higher

Quarterback remains the NFL's most valuable position , and teams are constantly searching for young passers with upside. Milton checks many of the boxes that intrigue personnel executives. He possesses elite arm strength, impressive athleticism, and flashes of playmaking ability that few quarterbacks can match physically.

Those traits were on full display against Arizona , where he turned limited opportunities into an eye-catching stat line. The problem for Dallas is that potential alone doesn't guarantee future success. Milton remains an unfinished product. One strong preseason performance does not erase concerns about his accuracy, decision-making, and overall readiness to lead an NFL offense over an extended period.

The Cowboys have to determine whether his long-term value to the organization exceeds what they could potentially receive from a quarterback-needy team. At the moment, the market may be more favorable than it has ever been.

Several teams could be interested

There is no shortage of franchises looking for answers at quarterback. The Cleveland Browns stand out as a potential destination. Although Deshaun Watson reportedly won the starting job entering the 2026 season, few around the league view him as a long-term solution. Shedeur Sanders remains a developing player, and Cleveland could benefit from adding another young quarterback with upside.

Milton would offer something different: a physically gifted passer without the baggage that has surrounded Watson or the intense scrutiny that follows Sanders. Other quarterback-needy teams could also view Joe as a worthwhile developmental project, especially if they believe they can refine his mechanics and decision-making.

For Dallas , that interest could translate into draft capital or other assets that better align with the team's immediate championship aspirations. Perhaps the strongest argument for trading Milton is the Cowboys' own evaluation of the quarterback room.

Despite Milton's impressive preseason showing, head coach Brian Schottenheimer has made it clear that the competition for the backup role remains close. "I think quite honestly, if you would just take the training camp competition, it's probably neck and neck, and Sam may be a little bit ahead," Schottenheimer said. That statement speaks volumes.

articles.title: Retirement of Kelli Finglass, the Dallas Cowboys' cheerleading director, is close and isn't up to Jerry Jones
articles.standfirst: After decades with Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, the longtime director says family could ultimately decide when she leaves
articles.summary: After decades with Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, the longtime director says family could ultimately decide when she leaves
articles.body:
After more than three decades shaping the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders , Kelli Finglass is no longer dismissing the idea that there will eventually be a life beyond the sideline.

The longtime director has become synonymous with the organization through years of auditions, television shows and difficult roster decisions, but she says the personal cost of that commitment has become harder to ignore.

“I have, but we’re so busy, we don’t have time to think about anything except the next hour,” Finglass told Vanity Fair when asked whether she has considered stepping away.

“It would be a personal decision. I’ve sacrificed a lot of time with my family.”

That admission is significant for someone whose professional life has been tied to the Cowboys for more than four decades.

Finglass first performed as a Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader from 1984 to 1989 before moving into coaching in 1991 and eventually becoming one of the most recognizable figures connected to the team.

One family milestone could change everything

Retirement doesn't appear imminent, but Finglass already knows what could make the decision feel right.

“My daughter is married, my son is in a relationship, and when I ever get the honor to be a grandma… I want that time if and when I have grandchildren,” she said. “That would definitely give me a heartfelt reason to go to a new chapter.”

Her perspective on leadership has also changed with age and motherhood.

Finglass said she spent much of her career trying to build flawless performances, only to learn through television that viewers often connect more deeply with honesty than perfection.

“I spent practically my whole career trying to create flawless performances, and what we’ve learned through TV is that vulnerability is actually more attractive,” she continued.

“People love when they can relate to somebody, and that’s been an unexpected ‘aha’ for me, for these girls to not project perfection, but rather be honest about their victories and honest about their struggles.”

America’s Sweethearts has changed what fans see

Netflix’s America’s Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders has expanded the spotlight around the team, giving viewers a closer look at the physical, emotional and personal demands placed on the women competing for spots.

That visibility has also amplified criticism online, something Finglass says can have a real effect.

“Words can hurt and they can also heal,” she said. “But the girls being busy and focused and supportive of each other is where our strength will remain.”

The series has been renewed for a fourth season in 2027 after its third season reached Netflix’s top 10 in 22 countries, ensuring Finglass still has another chapter ahead.

Her long-term future, though, now comes with an important caveat.

After spending decades helping build one of the most recognizable brands in sports entertainment, Finglass is increasingly willing to admit that family could one day matter more than staying in the role.

articles.standfirst: This will be Dak's 11th season with Dallas, but he has only won two playoff games in his career
articles.summary: This will be Dak's 11th season with Dallas, but he has only won two playoff games in his career
articles.body:
Entering the upcoming 2026 campaign, the Dallas Cowboys are eager to reverse a frustrating two-year playoff drought that stemmed not from their high-powered offense, but from a historically porous defense that ranked dead last in franchise history for points allowed per drive .

To fix those leaks, the front office brought in defensive coordinator Christian Parker , spent seven draft selections on defensive talent, and added veteran Von Miller to serve as a player-coach at 37 years old.

If this revamped unit can hold its ground, Dallas is primed to turn heads, especially with an offensive engine featuring Dak Prescott , running back Javonte Williams , and elite wideouts CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens .

Cowboys Coach Brian Schottenheimer’s Unique Team Bonding

So far, Dallas has looked sharp in winning its first two preseason matches , sparking optimism among fans that a cultural shift is underway. Much of that positive energy traces back to head coach Brian Schottenheimer , who recently treated quarterbacks Dak Prescott and Joe Milton , alongside their families, to an unexpected team-building outing learning how to do Greek dancing.

While lighthearted cultural excursions don't directly translate into X's and O's, they foster vital locker room chemistry.

Such unity is paramount for Schottenheimer, who enters his second year at the helm facing intense pressure; missing the postseason for a third consecutive year, and failing to reach the playoffs during his tenure, is a scenario owner Jerry Jones simply will not tolerate.

For Dak, this marks his 11th season in the NFL, and as the undisputed captain, he has set the bar impossibly high, boldly declaring this year absolute Super Bowl-or-bust territory .

Chasing History: Dak Prescott’s Record-Breaking Milestone Season

When the regular season kicks off, Prescott will cement his legacy as one of the greatest regular-season quarterbacks in Cowboys history . Statistically, he already stands as the franchise's all-time leader in passing yards ( 35,989 ).

This season, he is on the verge of claiming the record for most passing touchdowns in team history, sitting at 243 while Tony Romo holds the benchmark at 248 .

Furthermore, he is within striking distance of the 94 career wins shared by franchise legends Troy Aikman and Roger Staubach , as he currently stands at 83 victories .

The glaring hurdle remains January football, where across 10 seasons he holds a 2-5 playoff record , compounded by Dallas missing the postseason in consecutive years.

The Cowboys will look to start changing that narrative immediately when they host the New York Giants in the opening Sunday Night Football game of the year

articles.title: Micah Parsons' brother rubs salt in Cowboys' wounds with a message for Jerry Jones
articles.standfirst: One year after the trade to Green Bay, the bitterness surrounding Parsons’ departure remains
articles.summary: One year after the trade to Green Bay, the bitterness surrounding Parsons’ departure remains
articles.body:
A year has passed since Micah Parsons left the Dallas Cowboys , but the bitterness surrounding that breakup is clearly not gone.

On the anniversary of one of the most memorable images from Parsons’ final days in Dallas, his brother Terrence Parsons Jr. reposted a photo of the linebacker lying on a trainer’s table during a preseason game against the Atlanta Falcons and added a pointed message.

“Best thing Micah ever did to get the F outta there,” Terrence wrote.

The photo became symbolic of the contract standoff between Parsons and the Cowboys , even though Parsons insisted at the time that the moment had been misread. He said he had been dealing with back stiffness and pushed back against suggestions that he was disrespecting teammates.

“The way media shapes perception and narratives is wild–and if he hadn’t said anything, everyone would’ve just run with it,” Parsons wrote at the time. “I’d never disrespect the guys out there fighting for their lives.”

Micah Parsons’ Cowboys exit still clearly stings

The tension did not end with that preseason game.

Dallas had selected Parsons with the No. 12 pick in the 2021 NFL Draft, and he quickly became one of the league’s most disruptive defenders. In four seasons with the Cowboys , he totaled 256 tackles, 52.5 sacks and 63 tackles for loss while earning Defensive Rookie of the Year honors and three All-Pro selections.

By 2025, however, contract negotiations had broken down. Reports indicated that Jerry Jones and Parsons had come close to an agreement before discussions involving agent David Mulugheta complicated the process.

Six days after the trainer’s-table episode, the Cowboys traded Parsons to the Green Bay Packers for Kenny Clark and two first-round picks.

Terrence made his frustration clear then, too. He posted “just a point it never had to get to” and later described the situation as “Generational player mismanagement.”

His latest post suggests that view has not softened.

Parsons now has a possible Cowboys reunion in sight

The move to Green Bay gave Parsons the long-term deal he had been seeking, with the linebacker signing a four-year contract worth roughly $188 million.

He responded with another strong season, recording 41 tackles, 12.5 sacks and 12 tackles for loss in 14 games before suffering a torn ACL and meniscus damage in Week 15.

Now, the next chapter could be especially dramatic.

Parsons has been rehabilitating throughout the offseason and recently suggested that a Week 6 return against Dallas is not impossible.

“I think it’s very realistic,” Parsons said. “Me and the staff, we gotta put the work in.”

He added: “Is it possible? Yes. So I wouldn’t say it’s not possible... it’s not off the board, but we gotta put the work in.”

If that return happens against the Cowboys, the anniversary message from his brother will only add another layer to an already loaded reunion.

articles.title: Colin Cowherd rips Cowboys’ Super Bowl hype — And he has a point
articles.standfirst: Everyone wants to believe the Cowboys are Super Bowl contenders, but Colin Cowherd is pumping the brakes.
articles.summary: Everyone wants to believe the Cowboys are Super Bowl contenders, but Colin Cowherd is pumping the brakes.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys enter the 2026 season hoping to end a more than 30-year drought without winning a Super Bowl, a goal that team owner Jerry Jones has made a top priority. However, not everyone believes Dallas has what it takes to compete for a championship. One of the team’s biggest skeptics is renowned sports analyst Colin Cowherd, who believes the optimism surrounding the Cowboys is misplaced.

“They were 7-9-1 last year and awful against playoff teams… Don't convince yourself that average meal you ate at the restaurant was great because it's better than what you cook at home,” Cowherd said on his show, The Herd with Colin Cowherd .

The Cowboys have not lifted the Lombardi Trophy since the 1995 season. While they have reached the NFL playoffs several times over the past few decades, they have never been able to take the final step and return to the Super Bowl. To make matters worse, Dallas missed the postseason entirely in 2025 , further raising questions about the team’s championship chances this year.

Camden Brown giving Cowboys reason for optimism

Despite the skepticism, the Cowboys have found reasons for optimism during training camp. One of them is wide receiver Camden Brown , who has emerged as one of the team’s biggest surprises this summer. The young receiver, who joined Dallas as an undrafted free agent, has impressed the coaching staff and earned praise from former Cowboys star wide receiver Dez Bryant .

“Shoot, I just feel like I'm making the best of the opportunity whenever it comes my way,” Brown said, per the team. “I'm blessed to even say I'm in his locker room with a bunch of vets that's done it big. I feel like practice was really good, and that's just where it started. I start it from practice, and that's the preparation piece of it. So when I come out here, it slows down for me.”

“I feel like just stacking a week on top of a week, that's how I can make this team and keep doing what I got to do. So really, that's really what it is, for real,” he added.

Brown is fighting to secure a spot on the roster for Week 1 and has already showcased his potential during the preseason. In Dallas’ win over the Seattle Seahawks, he delivered a standout performance by catching two touchdown passes, strengthening his case to make the team.

The Cowboys will wrap up their NFL preseason schedule this Friday when they visit the New Orleans Saints , in their final tune-up before the start of the regular season.

articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys owner reminisced about the country music superstar and her charitable actions.
articles.body:
Practically the entire nation is in mourning this week following the passing of Dolly Parton . The legendary country music artist had a profound effect on the country and its citizens, as evidenced by the outpouring of tributes from all across the United States.

Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones is in that crowd, and he made sure to let people know how special Parton was while remembering her after her passing.

Jerry Jones says Dolly Parton donated $1 million to The Salvation Army after Thanksgiving Day performance in 2023

Jones chose to highlight, specifically, what she did outside of her music career . Her philanthropic efforts were well-known, and Jones chose to highlight that aspect of her life.

Truly one of the great role models of our country. She transcended being a great entertainer to a wonderful person. She's a role model to all of us. We're so thrilled that we got to have her here for our Thanksgiving Day kickoff. Never forget her giving a million dollars to The Salvation Army.

articles.title: Why former NFL Edge rusher believes the Dallas Cowboys are legitimate contenders in 2026
articles.standfirst: Could this finally be the Cowboys' year? One NFL analyst believes Dallas has everything it takes to end its 30-year Super Bowl drought.
articles.summary: Could this finally be the Cowboys' year? One NFL analyst believes Dallas has everything it takes to end its 30-year Super Bowl drought.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys enter the new season hoping to end a three-decade Super Bowl drought, backed by a revamped defense, a star-studded offense, and renewed confidence in Dak Prescott .

After finishing 7-9-1 and missing the playoffs last season, Dallas enters the year healthy and with one of the deepest rosters in the NFC , making the Cowboys a legitimate contender to compete for the championship.

Expectations are sky-high, with Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Javonte Williams, Jake Ferguson, Quinnen Williams, Demarvion Overshown , and Kenny Clark leading a team built to compete on both sides of the ball.

According to CBS analyst Leger Douzable , the Cowboys have everything they need to capture the Vince Lombardi Trophy for the first time since the 1995 season, largely because of their loaded offense.

“The Dallas Cowboys, I know every year people say, ‘This is our year!' This legitimately could be the year,” said Douzable.

“The offense is gonna be there. They literally retained everybody who was on offense, which is unheard of. They were able to do that.”

While Dallas' defense was its biggest weakness last season, the former NFL player believes the additions of Rashan Gary, Caleb Downs, and Malachi Lawrence , combined with the return of Quinnen Williams, could be enough to transform that unit.

“I really like what they have done. They refortified and revamped that defense, and just like the (Cincinnati) Bengals, we don't need you to be in the top five (on defense). We need you to be in the middle of the pack because your offense is explosive,” added Douzable, who played 10 seasons in the NFL.

The optimism is also shared by head coach Brian Schottenheimer , who has praised the roster’s overall depth and talent.

After missing the playoffs in each of the last two seasons, the Cowboys know there is little room for another disappointing campaign. The pressure is immense, and the expectations of a fan base that has waited 30 years to celebrate another championship have never been higher.

articles.title: Bold claim names George Pickens the undisputed star of the Dallas Cowboys
articles.standfirst: George Pickens hasn’t played a regular-season snap for the Cowboys yet, but one analyst believes he has already proven he’s the most dominant player in Dallas.
articles.summary: George Pickens hasn’t played a regular-season snap for the Cowboys yet, but one analyst believes he has already proven he’s the most dominant player in Dallas.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys entered training camp with a roster loaded with talent on both sides of the ball, but according to analyst and former team wide receiver Jesse Holley , one player stood out above everyone else and clearly separated himself from the pack: George Pickens .

According to Holley, Dallas’ new receiver was the most dominant player throughout training camp, showcasing a combination of talent, intensity, and commitment that impressed even those within the organization.

“It’s not even close,” Jesse Holley said multiple times. “And if either of you don’t say the same thing I’m about to say, you are absolutely lying to yourself. Far and away, the best player in training camp this year was George MF Pickens. Clear far away from the start to the finish. He played with energy, effort, enthusiasm… whatever you needed from him, George Pickens gave it to you.”

Pickens has always possessed the physical tools to become one of the NFL’s most dangerous wide receivers. His ability to win contested catches, beat coverage, and create explosive plays gives Dallas an offensive weapon capable of changing the dynamic of the team.

The Cowboys already have a superstar in CeeDee Lamb , but adding a fully focused Pickens could create one of the league’s toughest wide receiver duos to defend. Opposing defenses will have major problems covering both players, as committing too much attention to Lamb could leave Pickens in favorable one-on-one matchups.

With a healthier Lamb, it would not be surprising to see Pickens deliver a breakout season in 2026 and continue proving the potential he has shown since entering the NFL.

Dak Prescott recently highlighted the connection between his two top offensive weapons, praising the team-first mentality shared by both receivers.

“They truly want the other guy to have just as much success as each of them has individually, and they’re cheering each other on. They just got great personalities; they love to have fun, they love to compete, and I think just if you love the game of football and love to compete, the rest takes care of itself,” Prescott said.

With Prescott leading the offense, Lamb serving as the top target, and Pickens adding a new dimension to the attack, the Cowboys hope this combination can provide the boost they need to finally return to championship contention.

articles.title: Former Cowboys QB Tony Romo slapped with additional charges following July arrest
articles.standfirst: Tony Romo’s legal troubles are getting worse.
articles.summary: Tony Romo’s legal troubles are getting worse.
articles.body:
Legal troubles continue for former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo .

After his July arrest for driving under the influence in Wisconsin, the district attorney’s office added three new charges to the former NFL player’s case on Thursday.

According to TMZ , Romo received additional citations related to the incident. Court records show that the current CBS Sports broadcaster was charged with first-offense operating while intoxicated, as well as unsafe passing on the right side and having open intoxicants inside his vehicle.

The situation has also affected Romo professionally, as he was placed on indefinite leave from his role as CBS Sports’ lead NFL game analyst. The former quarterback signed a 10-year, $180 million contract with the network in 2020 , one of the most lucrative deals in sports broadcasting history.

“Tony Romo is on leave from his role at CBS Sports until further notice,” CBS Sports said in a prepared statement following his arrest. “JJ Watt will join Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson as CBS Sports ’ lead NFL team during Tony Romo’s absence. We will release the remainder of our NFL ON CBS roster at a later date.”

Tony Romo’s arrest shocked the NFL

Romo was arrested on July 23 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin , on suspicion of driving under the influence.

“Former Cowboys QB and CBS announcer Tony Romo was arrested overnight in Milwaukee on suspicion of operating while under the influence,” Ari Meirov of The 33rd Team wrote on his official X account. “Romo was pulled over yesterday around 8 p.m. and taken into custody after performing poorly on standard field sobriety tests. He’s due in court on Sept. 21.”

Romo played for the Cowboys from 2003 to 2016 , a span in which he was selected to four Pro Bowls and earned NFL All-Pro honors in 2014 .

Tony Romo faced legal trouble during a visit to his home state

Romo is a Wisconsin native and starred at Burlington High School before continuing his college career at Eastern Illinois.

During his high school years, Romo was also considered a standout basketball player. As a senior, he averaged 24.3 points, 8.8 rebounds, and 4.7 assists, while receiving offers from several Division I mid-major programs.

Romo joined the Cowboys as an undrafted free agent in 2003 and became the team’s full-time starting quarterback in 2006. During his 10 seasons as a starter, he led Dallas to the playoffs four times before losing his job to Dak Prescott in 2016 after suffering a back injury during the preseason.

Following that season, Romo announced his retirement and quickly transitioned into a successful broadcasting career.

In 13 NFL seasons, he set franchise records with 34,183 passing yards and 248 touchdowns. He also established league records for the most consecutive road games with a touchdown pass (41) and the most games in a single season with a passer rating above 135.0 (6).

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones was one of the few people to publicly defend Romo after his arrest.

“I’ve been talking to him … I love him, I love what he’s about, I love his character,” Jones said. “He’s a very, very unique talent, and the real question is, and I don’t even have to ask what the answer is, is do you think Tony Romo knows how to get up when he gets knocked down? He’s had a life of that. And that’s one of his greatest attributes. He can handle adversity and this is something that he will work through.”

articles.title: Jerry Jones and son Stephen Jones nearly came to blows after two of the Cowboys' most important decisions
articles.standfirst: Deion Sanders and Johnny Manziel triggered explosive arguments that ultimately shaped direction of the franchise
articles.summary: Deion Sanders and Johnny Manziel triggered explosive arguments that ultimately shaped direction of the franchise
articles.body:
Some of the most important decisions in Dallas Cowboys history were not made calmly around a conference table. At least twice, they pushed Jerry Jones and his son Stephen into confrontations intense enough to become personal, and, in one case, physical.

The first came in 1995, when Jerry was determined to sign Deion Sanders despite Stephen ’s concerns over the financial consequences.

The second arrived nearly 20 years later, when Johnny Manziel was still available in the first round of the 2014 NFL Draft and Jerry wanted the Cowboys to take a swing on the former Heisman Trophy winner.

Both moments revealed the same fault line inside the organization, pitting Jerry ’s appetite for bold, headline-making moves against Stephen ’s willingness to challenge him when he believed the risk was too great.

According to The Athletic, the Sanders argument became heated enough that Stephen shoved his father against a wall.

“You really gonna do this?” Stephen shouted, pressing his arm into Jerry’s chest. “What are you gonna do, hit me?” Jerry responded.

Jerry got his way. Dallas signed Sanders to a $35 million deal, and the star cornerback helped the Cowboys win the Super Bowl later that season.

The episode also reinforced something Jerry had already begun to understand about Stephen, in that he wasn't going to simply agree with him.

Johnny Manziel sparked another explosive argument

That dynamic returned during the 2014 draft. Manziel had fallen to Dallas at No.16, leaving Jerry with the opportunity to select one of the most famous and polarizing quarterbacks in the country.

Stephen opposed the move and helped steer the Cowboys toward Notre Dame guard Zack Martin instead. Jerry was furious with what he saw as a conservative choice.

“I hope you’re happy,” Stephen remembers his father telling him that night, face red, jaw clenched.

“You don’t do special things in life, I would have never bought the Dallas Cowboys , making middle-of-the-road decisions. And what you just did is down the middle. You’ll never be great.”

The years that followed made Stephen ’s argument look remarkably strong. Martin became a nine-time Pro Bowl selection and one of the best offensive linemen of his era.

Manziel , meanwhile, lasted only two NFL seasons, appearing in 14 games while throwing seven touchdown passes and seven interceptions.

Cowboys power struggle shaped major calls

The Sanders and Manziel stories show why the relationship between Jerry and Stephen Jones has never been a simple hierarchy.

Jerry ’s instinct to chase Sanders was vindicated almost immediately. Stephen’s resistance to Manziel proved equally significant.

That push and pull has helped define how Dallas has operated for decades.

“There’s a belief that sometimes Stephen is part of the mistakes Jerry makes,” former Dallas mayor and longtime Jones family friend Mike Rawlings said. “There’s also the belief that sometimes he saves Jerry’s ass.”

The Cowboys have made plenty of controversial decisions under the Jones family , but these two episodes stand out because of how close the disagreement came to boiling over.

One gamble produced a championship. One decision avoided a potential disaster. Both left a lasting mark on the franchise.

articles.title: Jerry Jones's succession plan for the Cowboys has a sad ending that leaves his son Stephen in a difficult situation
articles.standfirst: Jerry Jones has no plans to step aside, leaving Stephen Jones to prepare for an unexpected transition
articles.summary: Jerry Jones has no plans to step aside, leaving Stephen Jones to prepare for an unexpected transition
articles.body:
Jerry Jones has made it clear that he isn’t preparing to walk away from the Dallas Cowboys anytime soon.

At 83, the longtime owner still intends to remain involved until the day he’s no longer able to do so, leaving his son Stephen Jones facing an unusual challenge when that moment eventually arrives.

Jones bought the Cowboys for $140 million in 1989 and turned the franchise into one of the biggest commercial forces in professional sports.

Dallas is now valued at approximately $15.5 billion, according to Sportico, while Jones continues to hold the unusual combination of owner, president and general manager.

“I don’t have a succession plan, I don’t,” Jones told The Athletic. “One day I just won’t be here to toss my two cents in.”

Despite his admission that he has “no succession plan,” however, the man most likely to inherit significant control is already deeply embedded in the organization.

Stephen Jones has spent decades preparing for greater responsibility, overseeing areas including contracts, personnel and salary-cap strategy.

He’s become one of the most influential figures in the Cowboys' front office, working alongside his father while developing his own approach to running the team.

That creates a complicated situation for the younger Jones. He’ll eventually have to follow one of the most recognizable and influential owners in NFL history.

Stephen Jones could usher in a very different Cowboys era

Former Cowboys stars Troy Aikman and Darren Woodson both believe Dallas will look noticeably different once Stephen becomes the primary voice in the organization.

“I’m not pushing Jerry out by any means, but when that day comes, it’s going to feel a lot different,” said Aikman .

The Hall of Fame quarterback also believes Stephen’s lower-key personality could work in his favor. Unlike his father, Stephen doesn’t appear to crave the same level of attention, something Aikman thinks could serve him well.

Woodson sees another potential change. The former Dallas safety believes Jerry’s personal relationships with players can sometimes influence football decisions, allowing certain veterans more room than they might receive elsewhere.

He expects Stephen to be less forgiving when difficult choices have to be made.

That distinction could become increasingly important when Stephen eventually takes charge. He may be more inclined to make decisions based strictly on football and financial considerations rather than sentiment, potentially changing how the Cowboys handle contracts, roster turnover and personnel decisions.

Yet Stephen’s biggest challenge may have nothing to do with football operations. Jerry has been the face and voice of the Cowboys for almost 40 years, making his eventual absence impossible to overlook.

Jerry has also rejected suggestions that the franchise could simply be sold, despite occasional speculation about outside investors. The Cowboys are expected to remain within the Jones family.

That means Stephen should eventually have the opportunity to put his own stamp on the team. The transition, though, could be sudden.

articles.title: Jerry Jones sends Dak Prescott a clear message about his backup after the Cowboys preseason games
articles.standfirst: Prescott didn't play in any preseason games with the Cowboys, but he'll begin his 11th NFL season as a starter
articles.summary: Prescott didn't play in any preseason games with the Cowboys, but he'll begin his 11th NFL season as a starter
articles.body:
Did you know that since 2010 every NFL team in the NFC has played at least once in the Conference Championship game except for one? That team is the Dallas Cowboys ; the most valuable sports franchise in the whole world hasn't reached the doorstep of the Super Bowl since their last championship win in the 1995 season.

Confronting this frustrating drought, which includes a recent two-year playoff absence, star quarterback Dak Prescott has asserted that the current campaign is strictly " Super Bowl or bust, " noting that outside noise will always surround the franchise, so they might as well silence the critics by playing in the final game of the year.

Fixing the Defense and Cementing Dak Prescott's Legacy

The primary Achilles' heel for Dallas over recent seasons has been a leaky defensive unit, which last year ranked dead last in franchise history for points allowed per drive , prompting the front office to hire defensive coordinator Christian Parker and invest seven draft selections into defensive talent.

On the offensive side of the ball, anchored by Prescott, the major hurdle arrives once January hits, as his 2-5 postseason record contrasts sharply with his regular-season brilliance.

Following this 2026 season , Prescott is on track to cement his legacy as arguably the greatest regular-season signal-caller in franchise history.

Statistically, he already stands as the organization's all-time leader in passing yards with 35,989 , sits just behind Tony Romo’ s 243 to 248 touchdown passes , and his 83 wins leave him only 11 victories shy of the 94 wins jointly held by Troy Aikman and Roger Staubach.

Jerry Jones Hints at Keeping Both Sam Howell and Joe Milton

With Prescott securely entrenched as the starter for his 11th professional campaign , one of the most difficult 53-man roster decisions facing the front office involves sorting out the depth chart behind him between Sam Howell and Joe Milton .

Recognizing that injuries can derail a season at a moment's notice, franchise owner Jerry Jones offered a clear glimpse into the team's internal thinking following the preseason finale, hinting to ESPN that Dallas might bypass making a definitive cut. "That's one that we may just split the difference and have two backup quarterbacks here," Jones remarked.

While Howell held a slight edge during early training camp workouts under head coach Brian Schottenheimer, both signal-callers put together stellar summer performances, prompting Schottenheimer to label the competition as completely " neck and neck" .

Ultimately, the organization appears poised to retain both arms on the active roster, ensuring emergency depth behind Prescott.

articles.title: Haley Cavinder and Hanna Cavinder close out the Cowboys’ preseason with two looks that turned heads
articles.standfirst: The sisters arrived at AT&T Stadium.
articles.summary: The sisters arrived at AT&T Stadium.
articles.body:
T he Dallas Cowboys’ preseason came to an end and, amid all the action surrounding their final game, two appearances also drew attention away from the field. Haley Cavinder and Hanna Cavinder were at AT&T Stadium to support Jake Ferguson as Dallas wrapped up its preparation , but they did so in two looks that blended the sporting atmosphere with their own personal style.

Haley Cavinder keeps it simple for the final night

For the final preseason night, Haley opted for a simple look with details that fit the stadium setting. She wore a white dotted top, light-wash jeans, white heels and a matching bag, while keeping her hair in its natural style .

Hanna Cavinder goes for an all-white look

Alongside her sister, Hanna chose a different approach while maintaining a similar aesthetic. She appeared in white pants, matching heels and a white T-shirt featuring horse images, which she tied around her waist to create a shorter silhouette .

A white bag and her loose hair completed the outfit, making light tones the main feature of her look.

So, how did the Cowboys fare during the preseason?

On the field, the Cowboys finished with a 2-1 record. Their preparation began with a 17-7 win over the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field and continued with a 34-13 victory over the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium.

In their final game, the New Orleans Saints defeated Dallas 27-24 at AT&T Stadium .

Why didn’t Jake Ferguson play?

The decision not to use Jake Ferguson was not related to an injury. The tight end was given the night off along with several other starters, as the coaching staff opted to preserve key players ahead of the start of the regular season.

Now, Dallas has its sights set on the 2026 regular season, which will begin on September 13 when the Cowboys visit the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium.
